A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same ViP2-CLIP work. v2 ends with references without including its cited appendices; v3 supplies Appendices A–D. The retained method, results, and relocated analyses can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original anomaly-detection and segmentation results across 15 benchmarks, component ablations, and computational-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and additionally reports class-name sensitivity experiments, medical-data fine-tuning, prompt-length ablations, and detailed category-level results.

M1.justification: The ICA and FGP components, Top-k-based UTPA procedure, training losses, and inference aggregation remain unchanged. The redrawn diagrams and additional experimental details do not establish an algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: Evaluation retains the same seven industrial and eight medical benchmarks. Appendix C.2 additionally uses CVC-ColonDB or CVC-ClinicDB as medical auxiliary training data, modestly expanding training-domain coverage beyond the MVTec AD/VisA training reported in v2.

E2.justification: AA-CLIP joins the quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative comparison in Figure 4. Appendix C.1 also introduces PatchCore and RD4AD as full-shot comparators, with their scores explicitly sourced from AnomalyCLIP. This substantially broadens the comparison methods and training-data regimes represented.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a mixed industrial/medical auxiliary-training protocol, alternate auxiliary datasets when evaluating CVC-ColonDB, and a matched AnomalyCLIP control. New synonym-swap and prompt-length experiments also expand the evaluation procedures. The original Section 5.1 protocol remains unchanged; newly disclosed optimizer and preprocessing settings are documentation additions.

E4.justification: v3 supplies WinCLIP/AdaCLIP class-name sensitivity experiments, a static/dynamic prompt-length sweep, and an analysis of medical auxiliary training. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence. The state-adjective ablation is retained in Appendix C.3, with v2 Table 6 becoming v3 Table 9.

E5.justification: Both versions report detection metrics as point estimates and inference latency with ± values. The added AA-CLIP latency follows the existing practice; no new seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures are provided.

E6.justification: Original entries in Tables 1–5 and the relocated adjective ablation are unchanged. v3 adds baseline scores, full-shot comparisons, medical-fine-tuning results, category-level results, and anomaly maps. Table 3 now reports AA-CLIP inference at 19.17 ms versus the unchanged 48.69 ms for ViP2-CLIP, changing the fastest-inference ranking.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–11 retain the same substance. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs; the new applicability assumptions are informal limitations rather than formal theoretical developments.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about image-conditioned, class-name-free prompting, unified alignment, and strong generalization across 15 benchmarks. The conclusion preserves that scope; additional supporting experiments do not redefine the central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning contextual anomalies, cluttered or multi-object scenes, and fixed Top-k aggregation. It also adds interpretations of medical auxiliary training and prompt-length overfitting, and acknowledges AA-CLIP's inference-speed advantage. The new broad claim of matching or surpassing full-shot methods exceeds what Table 7 consistently supports.

D1.justification: Appendix B supplies essential details absent from v2: Adam with learning rate 0.001, 10 epochs, batch size 8, 518×518 resizing, OpenCLIP normalization, dataset sample counts, and baseline weight/reimplementation provenance. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Related work adds AA-CLIP and AF-CLIP, while the full-shot comparison adds PatchCore and RD4AD citations. These extend the research context without replacing the central positioning around class-name-independent prompting and unified alignment.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact, with localized rewrites and corrections. v3 organizes the added appendices and relocates the adjective ablation. It also introduces an incorrect Table 13 reference in the UTPA discussion, whose corresponding results remain in Table 5.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redrawn, Figure 4 gains an AA-CLIP row, and Tables 1–3 expand. New robustness plots, prompt-length heatmaps, detailed tables, and extensive anomaly-map galleries substantially expand the visual presentation. Several existing tables and the adjective ablation are relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies supporting sensitivity experiments and essential training details that v2 references but omits, substantially strengthening the central motivation and reproducibility. Additional comparisons, medical-adaptation analysis, and concrete limitations improve assessability. These gains outweigh localized defects, notably the overbroad full-shot interpretation in Appendix C.1/Table 7 and the incorrect Table 13 cross-reference. The improvement comes from stronger documentation and evidence, while the method and original scores remain stable.
